feat(CC-0116): scope service DB credentials per ControlPlane

Scope the Keystone service database credential per ControlPlane so two
ControlPlanes never share or clobber each other's DB credential on the
cluster-global OpenBao backend.

- Add a reconcileDBCredentials sub-reconciler that, in managed mode,
  projects a per-ControlPlane OpenBao-backed ExternalSecret named
  `{name}-keystone-db-credentials` in the ControlPlane namespace,
  reading the per-CP path `openstack/keystone/{namespace}/{name}/db`
  (scoped by both namespace and name) and owner-referenced to the CR
- Make the sub-reconciler a pure no-op in brownfield mode
  (database.clusterRef == nil): the user owns the DB-credential Secret
  out-of-band, so no ExternalSecret is projected and DBCredentialsReady
  is reported True immediately
- Add the DBCredentialsReady sub-condition to subConditionTypes and the
  metrics drift-guard map, and run the sub-reconciler after
  Infrastructure and before Keystone so the Keystone child is never
  projected before its DB-credential Secret exists
- Override the projected Keystone CR's database.secretRef to the
  operator-owned per-CP Secret (key "password") in managed mode, while
  leaving the source cp.Spec and the brownfield user-supplied secretRef
  untouched
- Add a dedicated dbCredentialsRequeueAfter (10s) backoff used while the
  ExternalSecret has not yet synced to Ready
- Seed the DB credential per ControlPlane at
  `openstack/keystone/{ns}/{name}/db` for each KORC_CONTROLPLANES
  identity in write-bootstrap-secrets.sh and drop the legacy flat
  `openstack/keystone/db` seed
- Remove the static production keystone-db ExternalSecret (deploy/eso),
  since managed ControlPlanes consume the operator-projected per-CP
  Secret instead
- Add a kind-only keystone-db ExternalSecret pinned to the default
  identity's per-CP path to keep standalone Keystone instances (Quick
  Start, keystone e2e/tempest/chaos suites) working
- Document in the eso-management / eso-control-plane OpenBao policies
  that the existing `openstack/*` read wildcards already cover the
  per-CP path, so no policy widening is required
- Assert create/update on externalsecrets in the c5c3-operator
  clusterrole/role Helm tests so reconcileDBCredentials may
  CreateOrUpdate the ExternalSecret
- Add unit tests covering managed ExternalSecret projection
  (store/data/owner-ref), the brownfield no-op, the ready/not-ready
  condition contract, and distinct per-CP remote keys and Secret names
- Add Keystone-projection tests asserting the managed secretRef
  override and the untouched brownfield secretRef
- Add integration tests for the DBCredentials gate blocking Keystone
  until the Secret syncs, the full managed-to-Ready path, and two
  ControlPlanes resolving to distinct DB-credential paths
- Add a presence-guarded db-credential-scoping chainsaw E2E suite
  asserting the projected ExternalSecret, materialised Secret, and
  DBCredentialsReady condition, and repoint the missing-secret,
  pod-security-restricted, and infra-stack-health fixtures to the
  per-CP OpenBao path
- Update the ControlPlane CRD, reconciler, OpenBao-bootstrap, Quick
  Start, and Keystone E2E reference docs to describe the operator-owned
  managed-mode database.secretRef, the per-CP DB path, and the reserved
  multi-DB form `openstack/keystone/{ns}/{name}/db/<dbname>`
